description: Default capability for the GameLib shell: core defaults plus the opener plugin (the shell.openExternal / steam:// parity path). Tauri v2 capabilities gate WEBVIEW->Rust IPC only; they are not consulted for Rust-side plugin API calls. The four app-defined relay commands (sidecar_invoke, sidecar_send, open_external, sidecar_store_snapshot) are registered via invoke_handler and do not require capability permissions. For the same reason the native file/folder picker (dialog.showOpenDialog parity, plan 30-03) needs NO dialog permission here: dispatch_rust_channel calls app.dialog().file() from Rust. Granting 'dialog:allow-open' would have exposed plugin:dialog|open directly to renderer JavaScript (including anything running in the store WebView surface) for zero benefit to the intended path — WR-03. notification:allow-is-permission-granted is the ONLY notification permission granted, and it is required, not optional: tauri-plugin-notification (added plan 33-04) auto-injects init-iife.js into every webview, which on non-Windows unconditionally invokes plugin:notification|is_permission_granted at load — without the grant that invoke is denied and crashes startup with an unhandled rejection. The full notification:default set is deliberately NOT granted (WR-03): real OS notifications go Rust-side via the notification_show relay (Rust plugin API calls bypass capabilities), and the frontend never uses window.Notification, so plugin:notification|notify / show / request_permission stay unexposed to the renderer. updater:default (plan 34-05) is required for the JS auto-update API surface (check()/downloadAndInstall()) added by tauri-plugin-updater; it is scoped to the plugin's own default command set, not a broader grant. shell:allow-execute is granted with an explicit allow-list entry scoped to ONLY {name: 'binaries/gamelib-sidecar', sidecar: true} (plan 34-05, T-34-09) -- this exposes execution of exactly the bundled sidecar externalBin to the webview's shell:default surface and nothing else; it deliberately does NOT grant an unscoped shell:allow-execute, which would let renderer JS launch arbitrary programs on the host.
